Subject: Follow-up: Horizon Health discovery — connectivity & compliance notes

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and to capture the asks we discussed: 

Pain points you flagged:
- Regulatory / data residency: patient PII must remain within your US datacenter and logs for audit need to be retained under your control.
- Network constraints: inference nodes cannot have unrestricted outbound internet access; limited outbound egress only to designated collectors.
- Air-gap preference in production for inferrers driven by board/regulatory guidance.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test results, and key management proofs required for procurement.

Goals we heard:
1) Run a short PoC (3–4 weeks) to validate latency and throughput on a small model footprint behind your network constraints.
2) Gather security evidence to move to legal/procurement.
3) Define a rollout plan that meets your residency and air-gap expectations.

Immediate next steps (owner suggestions):
- Emma/Horizon: provide an internal network diagram and the list of allowed egress endpoints (SFTP/collector IPs) — requested by Tue, Nov 24.
- Redwood: send our Private deployment architecture diagram and a network requirements template (attached).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Horizon infra + Redwood infra (30–45m). Proposed slots: Mon Nov 22 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue Nov 23 14:00–15:00 PT.

Attachments: redwood-private-arch.png, network-requirements-template.pdf (templates you can fill).

I’ll follow up with a tighter PoC plan after I get the network diagram.

Best,
Soojin Lee

From: Emma Thorne <emma.thorne@horizonhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Horizon Health discovery — connectivity & compliance notes

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful and accurate. A couple of clarifications and constraints from our security team: 

1) No outbound internet from inference nodes is allowed.
   - Egress must be limited to our log/metrics collector via SFTP over our managed appliance.
2) KMS/HSM: keys must be customer-controlled (Horizon-managed) and we need an HSM-backed solution or on-prem KMS integration.
3) Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II plus the last two pen-test summaries; they can be redacted but must show scope and findings.
4) Physical separation: we prefer an air-gapped topology for production (PoC can run in a controlled, peered environment).
5) Latency requirement: 95th percentile under 250ms for the expected 512-token avg workload.

On timing and procurement: we want a pricing ballpark for a 3-week PoC and an enterprise setup (3x GPU nodes) to feed into our procurement team. If possible, please include an estimate for time to produce the required security artifacts.

I’ll loop procurement once we have the PoC scope.

Emma Thorne
Director, Infrastructure Security | Horizon Health
emma.thorne@horizonhealth.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 12:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Horizon Health discovery — connectivity & compliance notes

Hi Emma — appreciate the specifics. Quick responses inline and a proposed path forward: 

On egress / network:
- We can configure Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments so inference hosts have no direct outbound internet.
- Logs/metrics can be exported only to your collector via a restricted SFTP egress point — we’ll work from your IP allowlist.

On KMS/HSM:
- We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and can provide an HSM-backed workflow. We’ll need details on your KMS (vendor, API, access pattern).

On evidence:
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and a pen-test summary. Estimated lead time to prepare redacted artifacts for your review is ~3 business days after procurement NDA.

On latency/POC sizing:
- For your 512-token workload, initial PoC config (2x A100-equivalent or 3x T4-equivalent depending on model) should meet the 95p 250ms target in a private environment; PoC plan will include a simple load script and perf checkpoints.

Ballpark pricing (high level) for PoC: $18k–$28k depending on exact GPU profile and on-site engineering support. Enterprise (3-node production-like) monthly run-rate estimate: $35k–$55k (committed capacity discount possible). We’ll provide a formal SOW/quote.

Proposed next step: technical deep-dive with your infra + security and our infra engineers. My proposed times still: Mon Nov 22 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue Nov 23 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works for your team?

I’ve attached the architecture diagram and network template again.

Best,
Soojin
